question:
**Choose the correct one-word substitute for:

A statement that is obviously true and needs no proof.**
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2 i.e. Axiom**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Axiom"** means a statement or proposition that is regarded as being self-evidently true, without the need for proof. (स्वयंसिद्ध सत्य)
 
 
• **Example:** The axiom "Parallel lines never meet" is a fundamental concept in geometry.
 
 
• An axiom is universally accepted as true and serves as a starting point for further reasoning or arguments.

**Correct word:** Axiom (स्वयंसिद्ध सत्य)

 
• **Example:** In mathematics, axioms are the foundation upon which theorems are built.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2 i.e. Axiom**.

---

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Maxim** (सूक्ति): A short, pithy statement expressing a general truth or rule of conduct.
 
 
• **Example:** "Honesty is the best policy" is a well-known maxim.
 
 

 
• **Proverb** (कहावत): A short, well-known saying that expresses a commonly held idea or belief.
 
 
• **Example:** "A stitch in time saves nine" is a famous proverb.
 
 

 
• **Epigram** (संक्षिप्त व्यंग्यात्मक कथन): A brief, witty, and often paradoxical statement or poem.
 
 
• **Example:** Oscar Wilde was known for his epigrams, such as "I can resist everything except temptation."
